title: BBDF and Noah's Hope: a careful first step for CLN3 and CLN2 families

sentences.text: At Beyond Batten Disease Foundation (BBDF), we support CLN3 families, while Noah's Hope supports families affected by CLN2 disease.
Both diseases involve material building up in lysosomes, the cell's recycling compartments.
The atlas also infers similar symptoms, but that comparison has confidence 0.4, below 0.5, so it is a starting point rather than proof of matching needs.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: The BDCRC longitudinal natural history study includes people with CLN3 disease and offers a starting point for discussing shared learning.
Other CLN3 resources include the International DEM-CHILD Database, the Natural History Study of Batten Disease, and the Batten Disease Clinical Research Consortium.
We propose exploring useful study information, not promising CLN2 eligibility or access to data.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please help confirm whether CLN2 also involves foveal atrophy, an undetectable dark-adapted electroretinogram, and central thinning of the retina's outer nuclear layer—the specific eye findings flagged for comparison.
We should check what CLN3 does, what material accumulates, and whether the study can appropriately include CLN2 families before offering participation.
The atlas's predictions that certain CLN3 and TPP1 variants remove protein function are unverified, inferred connections with confidence 0.45, below 0.5.
Let us jointly draft a short enquiry to the BDCRC study team asking whether and how study information or participation could be offered to CLN2 families.
What does the CLN3 protein do, and what exactly is stored?
CLN3's recorded roles in protein breakdown and lysosome organization rely on inferred annotations.
We propose a biochemist's review of recent structural and lipid studies before drawing stronger conclusions.
Dear Noah's Hope team,
I'm writing on behalf of BBDF to explore a modest collaboration.
CLN3 and CLN2 share evidence of lysosomal storage.
Could we draft an enquiry to the BDCRC study team together this month?
Let's check suitability before making any invitation to families.
Thank you for considering this.
[Your name], on behalf of Beyond Batten Disease Foundation (BBDF)
